papers.title_en: ReDIL-GNN: Resynthesis Domain Incremental Learning for Circuit Graph Neural Networks
papers.authors: Rupesh Raj Karn, Johann Knechtel, Ozgur Sinanoglu
papers.evidence: 面向逻辑重综合的电路图神经网络增量学习
papers.tldr: 逻辑再综合在保持电路功能的同时改变门类型、拓扑与结构统计，导致电路GNN出现域偏移而任务标签不变。ReDIL-GNN面向该设定，固定预测或表示头并增量适配新综合风格，同时评估旧域保持。其提出RAI预适配评分，综合适配需求、源等价可恢复性、结构覆盖与更新兼容性。实验覆盖硬件安全分类和表示学习，RAI能区分不支持与有前景的更新，将再综合感知学习转为部署控制回路。
papers.abstract_en: Logic resynthesis preserves circuit functionality while changing gate vocabulary, topology, and structural statistics, creating domain shift for circuit graph neural networks (GNNs) without changing task labels. To study this setting, we introduce ReDIL-GNN, a resynthesis domain-incremental learning framework that adapts a fixed prediction or representation head as new synthesis styles arrive and evaluates retention on all previously observed domains. Because not every shift should be adapted blindly, ReDIL-GNN further introduces the Resynthesis Adaptability Index (RAI), a pre-adaptation score that combines adaptation need, source-equivalence recoverability, structural coverage, and update compatibility. We evaluate supervised hardware-security tasks and representation-learning models using task-native metrics for classifiers and source-equivalence retrieval metrics for embedding models, comparing naive fine-tuning with LwF, Online EWC, MAS, ER, A-GEM, DER++, ER+LwF, and equivalence-guided replay. Across the studied pipelines, RAI separates unsupported shifts from promising updates, ranging from 0.001 for a structurally uncovered GNN-RE ABC-rewrite shift to 0.824 for the best original-only GNN-RE adaptation case. In practice, ReDIL-GNN turns resynthesis-aware circuit learning into a deployment control loop: RAI screens each new synthesis flow before update, guiding whether to reuse the current model, apply retention-aware adaptation, or defer adaptation until the shift is better supported.

papers.title_en: SCHERI: Provably Secure Speculation Under the Constant-Time Policy for CHERI (Extended Version)
papers.authors: Shixin Song, Davide Davoli, Elias Storme, Marton Bognar, Dominique Devriese, Frank Piessens, Tamara Rezk
papers.evidence: 面向能力安全、推测执行与信息流安全的形式化框架
papers.tldr: CHERI 等能力架构能隔离软件组件，但推测执行可能破坏常量时间程序的保证并瞬态泄露隔离秘密。本文先揭示为 CHERI 提供安全推测并非易事，现有方案无法保持机密性。作者提出联合推理能力安全、推测执行与信息流安全的形式化框架，并基于该框架设计新处理器 SCHERI。SCHERI 被形式化证明能为常量时间策略提供端到端安全推测保证，为抗 Spectre 的未来能力处理器提供理论基础与实践指导。
papers.abstract_en: Capability-based architectures such as CHERI provide strong support for the architectural isolation of software components. To additionally protect against microarchitectural leakage, software can be written in a constant-time fashion. Modern processors, however, rely heavily on speculative execution, which can invalidate the constant-time guarantees and leak isolated secrets transiently.   In this work, we show that providing secure speculation for CHERI is non-trivial, and that existing proposals fail to preserve the confidentiality guarantees. We develop a formal framework for reasoning jointly about capability safety, speculative execution, and information-flow security, and use it to demonstrate potential leaks. We then present SCHERI, a new processor design within this framework, and formally prove that it provides end-to-end secure speculation guarantees for the constant-time policy.   Our results provide formal foundations and practical guidance for building future capability-based processors, which are resilient to Spectre attacks for constant-time programs.

papers.title_en: MAGS: Multi-agent Auto-formalization Guarantees Safety for Agentic Outputs
papers.authors: Albert Wu, Nicholas Roberts, Tzu-Heng Huang, Haoran Lin, Gil Friedman, Sungjun Cho, Gabriel Orlanski, Frederic Sala
papers.evidence: 基于LLM的多智能体框架，通过Dafny验证中间表示生成带形式安全保证的程序
papers.tldr: 针对LLM编码智能体生成程序规模过大、人工审查难以覆盖所有边界情况的问题，本文提出统一多智能体框架MAGS，利用Dafny作为可验证的中间表示，将程序自动形式化并机械检查安全属性。该框架在生成阶段即给出形式化安全保证，弥补了模糊测试、静态分析与LLM作为验证器覆盖不足的缺陷。其核心思想是让LLM自动完成规范与证明工程，为软件形式验证提供可迁移的自动化范式，对硬件形式验证同样具有方法借鉴意义。
papers.abstract_en: LLM coding agents now generate complex programs at a scale that makes thorough human review increasingly difficult, raising the risk of safety and security failures. Common approaches, including fuzz testing, static analysis, and LLM-as-a-Verifier, can detect many failures but struggle to cover all possible edge cases. Formal verification addresses this by providing machine-checkable guarantees over specified properties, but traditionally demands substantial manual specification and proof engineering. We introduce a unified multi-agent framework, MAGS, that generates executable programs with formal safety guarantees, using Dafny as a verification-aware intermediate representation where safety properties can be mechanically checked. MAGS formalizes and freezes human-audited APIs and safety requirements, translates generated code into Dafny, repairs violations using verifier feedback, and compiles verified programs back into executable code. We evaluate MAGS on 100 CUDA kernels, 100 terminal scripts, and 20 robotic-arm tasks. Across all 220 examples, it achieves a 100% success rate in producing programs with non-trivial safety guarantees against frozen specifications. Independent safety and functional evaluations further show strong performance across all three domains, while revealing failures when the auto-formalized semantics do not fully capture the target behavior.

papers.title_en: Long-horizon autoformalization of a core theorem underlying MIP* = RE
papers.authors: Sirui Lu, Ruixuan Deng, Yanqiao Zhu, Zhengfeng Ji
papers.evidence: AI证明智能体用于长时程形式化定理证明
papers.tldr: 大型数学形式化常需专家团队数年，长周期自动形式化还面临陈述漂移与证明组合难题。FormalFlow 以共享蓝图协调 AI 证明智能体，在人类监督下进行嵌套规划、证明与审查循环，并持续强化验证。它完成 MIP*=RE 核心定理——经典低个体度测试量子可靠性——的 Lean 4 机器验证证明，耗时 63 天，产出 126,367 行 Lean 代码。该工作纠正了边条件与中间错误，保留原最终误差界，并为小团队可负担地验证重大研究证明提供路径。
papers.abstract_en: Landmark mathematical formalizations have taken specialist teams years to complete. We present FormalFlow, a system that coordinates AI proving agents under human supervision to address statement drift and proof composition in long-horizon formalization. Drawing on software engineering principles and practices, it uses a shared blueprint to guide nested planning, proving and review loops. Agents strengthen verification and review throughout formalization. We completed a machine-checked Lean 4 proof of the quantum soundness of the classical low individual-degree test, a core theorem underlying MIP* = RE. Developing the proof took 63 days; greater parallelism could further reduce this time. The final library contains 126,367 lines of Lean code, all generated by agents. The formalization corrects side conditions and intermediate errors while preserving the published final error bound under corrected assumptions. This work provides a verified foundation for quantum complexity and demonstrates a route to affordable verification of major research proofs by small teams.
